hints: Express the forward driving force $F_D$ of the car in terms of power $P$ and speed $v$ using $P = F_D v$.

Since the car moves up the hill at constant speed, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the driving force balances the total opposing force down the hill: the resistance of $600\text{ N}$ plus the component of weight $mg\sin\theta$.
Substitute $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin\theta = 0.1$, and $P = 22500\text{ W}$, then solve for $v$ to show that $v = 11.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula relating mechanical power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D v$$
Rearrange to express driving force $F_D$ in terms of power and speed:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$
Substitute $P = 22500\text{ W}$:
$$F_D = \frac{22500}{v}$$

Identify the forces acting parallel to the inclined plane. The driving force $F_D$ acts up the hill. Opposing motion down the hill are the constant resistance force $R = 600\text{ N}$ and the component of weight parallel to the slope $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta$.

State Newton's second law along the incline:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
Because the car travels at a constant speed, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - mg\sin\theta - R = 0$$

Substitute the numerical values $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin\theta = 0.1$, and $R = 600\text{ N}$:
$$\frac{22500}{v} - (1400)(10)(0.1) - 600 = 0$$
Calculate the weight component:
$$(1400)(10)(0.1) = 1400\text{ N}$$
Combine the opposing forces:
$$\frac{22500}{v} - 1400 - 600 = 0$$
$$\frac{22500}{v} - 2000 = 0$$
$$\frac{22500}{v} = 2000$$

Multiply both sides by $v$ and divide by $2000$ to solve for $v$:
$$v = \frac{22500}{2000} = 11.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the speed of the car is $11.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, as required.

hints: Calculate the driving force at the instant the car enters the new section using $F_D = \frac{P}{v}$ with $P = 22500\text{ W}$ and $v = 11.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
On the new incline of $2^\circ$, calculate the new component of weight acting down the slope: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 2^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law up the slope: $F_D - mg\sin 2^\circ - 600 = ma$, and solve for the initial acceleration $a$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force $F_D$ exerted by the car engine at the start of this section using $P = F_D v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v}$$
Substitute $P = 22500\text{ W}$ and the current speed $v = 11.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{22500}{11.25} = 2000\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting parallel to the new $2^\circ$ incline:
- Driving force up the hill: $F_D = 2000\text{ N}$
- Resistance down the hill: $R = 600\text{ N}$
- Weight component down the hill: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin 2^\circ$

State Newton's second law along the direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$F_D - mg\sin 2^\circ - R = ma$$
Substitute $F_D = 2000\text{ N}$, $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $R = 600\text{ N}$:
$$2000 - (1400)(10)\sin 2^\circ - 600 = 1400a$$
Combine the numerical constants:
$$2000 - 600 - 14000\sin 2^\circ = 1400a$$
$$1400 - 14000\sin 2^\circ = 1400a$$

Evaluate the trigonometric term and simplify the left-hand side:
$$14000\sin 2^\circ \approx 14000(0.0348995) = 488.593\text{ N}$$
$$1400 - 488.593 = 911.407\text{ N}$$
$$1400a = 911.407$$

Divide both sides by the mass $1400\text{ kg}$ to find the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{911.407}{1400} \approx 0.651005\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to three significant figures:
$$a = 0.651\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
